qt: to the Commission Carolina Morace (The Left), Valentina Palmisano (The Left), Mario Furore (The Left), Danilo Della Valle (The Left) Subject:

The education rights of Palestinian minors are being drastically curtailed by Israel’s military operations in Gaza and its policies in the West Bank. The UN has stated that, as of September 2026, around 200 000 children still did not have any access to structured learning in Gaza, adding that much of the area’s schools have been damaged or destroyed. Access to education is hindered on a daily basis in the West Bank by a combination of school demolitions, settler attacks and Israeli policies restricting freedom of movement. In the first half of 2026 alone, these and other education-related incidents had a direct impact on more than 20 000 pupils and students. Though the EU funds the Palestinian education system, these endeavours are no substitute for addressing the underlying causes preventing children from going to school. In view of the above: 1.

How has the Commission gone about calling on the Israeli Government to uphold the education rights of Palestinian minors and to put a stop to the practices that are preventing Palestinians from exercising these rights?
Were these violations to persist, will the Commission propose measures that will bring about a significant shift in EU-Israel relations?

What financial resources will the Commission commit to rebuilding and protecting Palestinian schools, and what has it done to obtain compensation from the Israeli authorities for the damage caused to EU-funded educational facilities?
